subject: Affordability roadmap — mini MAP & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.j@clearpay.com>, Dan Brewster <dan.brewster@clearpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Affordability roadmap — mini MAP & next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciate how candid you were about spend volatility and the ops constraints. Quick recap from our call and a suggested mini MAP (mutual action plan) so we’re aligned on concrete next steps.

Top takeaways (pain + constraints)
- Predictable token spend is the blocker for launch: infra + compliance team need a 3–6 month runway cap to sign off.
- Peak inference latency must stay <= 220ms for customer-facing flows — you can tolerate small increases during off-peak batch windows.
- Current budget target: keep inference run-rate under $18k/mo for the pilot (volume ~120M tokens/month).
- Ops: limited SRE cycles for complex deployment work; pref you'd prefer Redwood-managed pilot with a defined rollback window.

What Redwood proposes (mini MAP / pilot scope)
- 6-week scoped pilot (hosted) with 3 phases: 1) baseline telemetry & modeling (1 week) 2) batching + prefix cache integration (3 weeks) 3) quantization/variant A/B (2 weeks).
- Goal: demonstrate >=30% per-token cost reduction at 120M tokens/month without exceeding latency SLO for 95th pct.
- Deliverables: cost sensitivity model, runbook for rollback, and an ops-lite deployment plan.

Immediate asks from your side
- Share a 2-week sample of traffic (anonymized) — token-level distribution and percentiles by endpoint.
- Confirm the internal reviewers (procurement + security) and their approval SLAs.
- Permission to run a small synthetic load during week 1 to validate latency profiles.

Budget/ROI framing (quick view)
- Baseline (your numbers): ~120M tokens/mo -> est $24k/mo using standard hosted throughput (no batching).
- Target (with batching + prefix cache): ~30–40% reduction -> ~$14.4–16.8k/mo (hits your $18k target).
- Upside: selective quantization on non-customer-facing paths could add another ~10–15% savings; we only enable after QA signoff.

Attachments: mini-MAP-draft.pdf (MAP timeline + responsibilities), token-modeling-sheet.xlsx (sensitivity scenarios).

Next steps
- If that looks right, I’ll: 1) send a short SOW-lite for the pilot, 2) drop a calendared 30-min checkpoint for next Tuesday (Sep 8), and 3) request the traffic snapshot.

Thanks — happy to tighten any part of the plan.

—Naomi

From: Claire Johnson <claire.j@clearpay.com>

Cc: Dan Brewster <dan.brewster@clearpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Affordability roadmap — mini MAP & next steps

Thanks, Naomi — very clear and useful. Couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Budget framing — our execs set a conservative cap for any new infra spend. The $18k/mo is the upper bound for pilot approval; below $15k/mo makes procurement comfortable.
2) Volume nuance — 120M tokens/mo is an aggressive peak; realistic expected average for pilot is ~80–90M tokens/mo but bursty. Would Savage (our SRE lead) be okay with synthetic load during off-peak?
3) Security — we need to see where data retention and audit logs appear in the MAP; SOC2 evidence is a gating item.

Would appreciate the SOW-lite and a one-page cost sensitivity that shows 80M, 100M, and 120M scenarios with batching turned on/off. If you can surface a best/worst case and the assumptions, we’ll route to procurement.

Claire
Claire Johnson | Head of Product
Clearpay

Claire — thanks for the quick read. Attached is a 1-page sensitivity table (also pasted below) and a slightly revised MAP that calls out retention/audit deliverables for week 1. I pulled conservative latency assumptions to respect the 95th pct SLO.

Sensitivity (hosted runs, baseline kernels)
- 80M tokens/mo: baseline est $16k/mo; with batching + prefix cache -> $10.5k–$11.2k (35–40% savings).
- 100M tokens/mo: baseline est $20k/mo; with batching + prefix cache -> $13k–$14k (30–35% savings).
- 120M tokens/mo: baseline est $24k/mo; with batching + prefix cache -> $14.4k–$16.8k (30–40% savings).

Key assumptions
- Batching effectiveness depends on percent of short, similar-prefix requests; we used a conservative 25–35% batching hit rate for modeling.
- Prefix cache gives an additional ~5–12% effective token reduction on heavy conversational flows.
- Quantization/variant switching is applied only to background/async endpoints. We model a further 10% optional saving when enabled.

Security & compliance callouts
- Week 1 deliverable: SOC2 evidence map and retention policy draft (we’ll provide sample audit logs and KMS integration notes).
- We’ll run everything under Redwood’s hosted sandbox and enable data redaction; if you need a VPC option we can scope that as an add-on.

Proposed SOW-lite items I’ll include in the doc:
- Scope, success criteria (cost reduction & latency SLO), timeline, rollback plan, and point contacts.
- Fixed pilot fee + capped run-rate help us absorb initial setup; we’ll propose a trial fee that nets to $0–$3k for you if you commit to a 90-day evaluation.

If that aligns I’ll: 1) upload the SOW-lite to the Drive link I shared, 2) send a short calendar invite for Sep 8 checkpoint, and 3) request the anonymized 2-week traffic dump.

—Naomi
